stem: Training jobs are expensive, and many can tolerate interruption. Which TWO actions reduce cost? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Keep every experiment's endpoint running indefinitely
Use the largest GPU instance for all small experiments
Disable checkpointing to reduce S3 storage usage
Use managed spot training with checkpoints
Stop idle notebooks and development endpoints automatically

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Spot training and stopping idle resources remove major sources of waste.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Keep every experiment's endpoint running…: Idle endpoints cost money.
• Use the largest GPU instance for all small…: Oversized instances waste money.
• Disable checkpointing to reduce S3 storage usage: No checkpoints makes Spot interruptions costly.

Key takeaway: Cut ML costs with Spot and idle-resource cleanup.

stem: A deep learning inference workload needs high throughput at lower cost than GPUs. Which instance option may fit?

choices.text: Memory optimized X2 instances
AWS Inferentia-based instances (Inf2)
Burstable T3 instances with credits
Storage optimized I4i instances

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Inferentia instances are designed for cost-efficient, high-throughput inference.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Memory optimized X2 instances: Memory optimized targets RAM.
• Burstable T3 instances with credits: Burstable instances are not for sustained inference.
• Storage optimized I4i instances: Storage optimized targets I/O.

Key takeaway: Cost-efficient inference accelerators → Inferentia.

stem: A team wants to see which SageMaker resources drive ML costs by project. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Store all models in a single S3 prefix
Delete all ML resources at the end of each month and recreate them
Tag SageMaker resources and use cost allocation tags in Cost Explorer
Use one shared role name for every project

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Cost allocation tags attribute costs to projects in Cost Explorer.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Store all models in a single S3 prefix: Prefixes do not attribute compute costs.
• Delete all ML resources at the end of each…: Deleting resources does not attribute costs.
• Use one shared role name for every project: Role names are not cost attribution.

Key takeaway: Attribute ML costs with tags.

stem: A GPU endpoint serves a large model, but traffic drops to near zero at night. Which change reduces cost while keeping daytime performance?

choices.text: Auto scaling with scheduled or target tracking policies, scaling in at night
Deleting the endpoint every morning and recreating it at night
Moving the model to a CPU instance during the day for savings
Keeping the same peak instance count running 24 hours a day, every day of the week

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Scaling in during low traffic avoids paying for idle capacity.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Deleting the endpoint every morning and…: The schedule is backward and disruptive.
• Moving the model to a CPU instance during…: CPUs may miss daytime latency targets.
• Keeping the same peak instance count running…: Peak capacity all day wastes money.

Key takeaway: Scale endpoints with traffic patterns.

stem: Training jobs must not access the internet and must reach S3 only through private networking. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Run training in a VPC with network isolation and S3 VPC endpoints
Store training data in a public bucket for fast access
Disable encryption so data loads faster from S3
Run the training jobs in public subnets that route through an internet gateway

explanation:
Why this is correct:
VPC mode with network isolation and endpoints keeps traffic private.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Store training data in a public bucket for…: Public buckets expose data.
• Disable encryption so data loads faster from S3: Disabling encryption weakens security.
• Run the training jobs in public subnets that…: Public subnets allow internet access.

Key takeaway: Private training with VPC mode and endpoints.

stem: A regulated company requires model artifacts, training volumes, and endpoint storage encrypted with keys it controls. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Rely on unencrypted storage protected by IAM policies only
Specify customer managed KMS keys for training, outputs, and endpoints
Encrypt artifacts manually on a laptop before each upload
Store the model artifacts in a public bucket with long, obscure object names

explanation:
Why this is correct:
SageMaker supports customer managed KMS keys for volumes, outputs, and endpoints.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Rely on unencrypted storage protected by IAM…: IAM does not replace encryption.
• Encrypt artifacts manually on a laptop…: Manual encryption is error-prone.
• Store the model artifacts in a public bucket…: Public buckets expose artifacts.

Key takeaway: Encrypt ML assets with customer managed keys.

stem: Distributed training nodes exchange data, and security requires that traffic between containers be encrypted. Which setting fits?

choices.text: Enable debugger hook collection
Increase the job's volume size
Enable managed spot training for the job
Enable inter-container traffic encryption

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Inter-container traffic encryption protects data exchanged between training nodes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Enable debugger hook collection: Debugger hooks collect tensors.
• Increase the job's volume size: Volume size is unrelated.
• Enable managed spot training for the job: Spot is a cost option.

Key takeaway: Encrypt distributed training traffic.

stem: Data scientists need different permissions for notebooks, training, and deployment, following least privilege. Which feature helps create these roles?

choices.text: IAM users with long-term keys in notebooks
The account root user shared among the team
SageMaker Role Manager personas and activities
A single AdministratorAccess role for everyone

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Role Manager helps build least-privilege roles for ML personas and activities.

Why the other options are wrong:
• IAM users with long-term keys in notebooks: Long-term keys in notebooks are insecure.
• The account root user shared among the team: Root sharing is insecure.
• A single AdministratorAccess role for everyone: Admin access violates least privilege.

Key takeaway: Build ML personas with Role Manager.

stem: Applications in a VPC must call a SageMaker endpoint without traversing the internet. Which feature fits?

choices.text: An interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker Runtime API
A public IP address on each client instance
A NAT gateway route for all SageMaker calls
An internet gateway attached to private subnets

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) provide private access to the SageMaker Runtime API.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A public IP address on each client instance: Public IPs expose instances.
• A NAT gateway route for all SageMaker calls: NAT routes over the internet.
• An internet gateway attached to private subnets: IGWs make subnets public.

Key takeaway: Private endpoint invocation → interface VPC endpoints.

stem: Auditors ask who deployed or updated models and endpoints last quarter. Which source provides this?

choices.text: Feature Store offline store tables
CloudTrail records of SageMaker API calls
Model Monitor data quality reports
CloudWatch endpoint latency metrics

explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudTrail records API calls such as CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint with the caller identity.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Feature Store offline store tables: Feature tables store features.
• Model Monitor data quality reports: Monitor reports cover data.
• CloudWatch endpoint latency metrics: Metrics do not show who acted.

Key takeaway: Audit ML actions with CloudTrail.

stem: Which TWO controls protect sensitive training data in S3? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disabling S3 Block Public Access to simplify policies
Storing access keys in the bucket's object metadata
Public read access for easy sharing with partners
SSE-KMS encryption with a customer managed key
Bucket policies restricting access to specific roles and VPC endpoints

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Restrictive bucket policies and KMS encryption protect training data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disabling S3 Block Public Access to simplify…: Disabling Block Public Access risks exposure.
• Storing access keys in the bucket's object…: Keys in metadata are insecure.
• Public read access for easy sharing with…: Public access exposes data.

Key takeaway: Restrict access and encrypt training data.

stem: A company must document each production model's intended use, training data, evaluation results, and risks for governance. Which feature fits?

choices.text: SageMaker Studio themes
SageMaker Canvas charts
SageMaker Model Cards
SageMaker Debugger rules

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Model Cards document model details, intended use, evaluation, and risks.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SageMaker Studio themes: Themes are UI settings.
• SageMaker Canvas charts: Canvas charts visualize data.
• SageMaker Debugger rules: Debugger inspects training.

Key takeaway: Document models with Model Cards.

stem: A real-time endpoint shows rising ModelLatency after a new version was deployed, while traffic is unchanged. What should the team do first?

choices.text: Delete the CloudWatch log groups so that monitoring overhead is reduced
Retrain the model on more data before investigating the latency change
Compare the new version's resource usage and latency with the previous version and roll back if needed
Increase the endpoint's data capture percentage to 100% so that every request and response is recorded

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Comparing versions isolates the regression; rolling back restores service while investigating.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delete the CloudWatch log groups so that…: Deleting logs removes evidence.
• Retrain the model on more data before…: Retraining does not address latency regression.
• Increase the endpoint's data capture…: More capture adds overhead.

Key takeaway: Investigate regressions by comparing versions; roll back if needed.

stem: A model degrades each holiday season and recovers afterward. Which maintenance strategy fits?

choices.text: Stop serving predictions during holidays and resume in January
Include seasonal data in training and schedule retraining or seasonal models ahead of holidays
Increase the endpoint instance size during the holiday season only
Freeze the current model permanently, because the seasonal degradation is only temporary each year

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Seasonal data and planned retraining address predictable drift.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Stop serving predictions during holidays and…: Stopping service harms the business.
• Increase the endpoint instance size during…: Larger instances do not fix accuracy.
• Freeze the current model permanently,…: Freezing ignores known degradation.

Key takeaway: Plan for seasonal drift.

stem: Batch predictions run nightly on an always-on real-time endpoint that is idle during the day. Which change reduces cost?

choices.text: Enable data capture on the real-time endpoint
Add more instances to the real-time endpoint
Use a larger instance for the real-time endpoint
Use batch transform jobs for the nightly predictions

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Batch transform runs only when needed, avoiding idle endpoint costs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Enable data capture on the real-time endpoint: Data capture adds cost.
• Add more instances to the real-time endpoint: More instances cost more.
• Use a larger instance for the real-time endpoint: Larger instances cost more.

Key takeaway: Use batch transform for scheduled offline scoring.

stem: A model endpoint receives requests from a public web app. Which TWO measures protect the endpoint? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Put API Gateway with authentication and throttling in front of the backend
Make the endpoint callable anonymously to reduce latency
Share the endpoint's execution role with the web users
Embed IAM access keys in the web page's JavaScript so browsers can call the endpoint directly
Invoke the endpoint only from a backend with IAM credentials, not from browsers

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Server-side invocation with IAM plus an authenticated, throttled API layer protects the endpoint.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Make the endpoint callable anonymously to…: SageMaker endpoints cannot be safely exposed anonymously.
• Share the endpoint's execution role with the…: Sharing roles with users is insecure.
• Embed IAM access keys in the web page's…: Embedded keys leak.

Key takeaway: Front model endpoints with authenticated APIs.

stem: Which setting controls how often Model Monitor analyzes captured data?

choices.text: The S3 bucket's lifecycle rules only
The endpoint's instance count setting
The training job's max runtime value
The monitoring schedule's cron expression

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Monitoring schedules define how often monitoring jobs run.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The S3 bucket's lifecycle rules only: Lifecycle rules manage storage.
• The endpoint's instance count setting: Instance count affects capacity.
• The training job's max runtime value: Max runtime limits training.

Key takeaway: Configure monitoring frequency with schedules.

stem: A large language model endpoint's cost is dominated by GPU time. Which TWO optimizations reduce cost per request? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disable caching of repeated prompt prefixes
Quantize the model where accuracy allows
Increase maximum output tokens for every request
Deploy one endpoint per user to isolate traffic
Use optimized serving with batching of requests

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Quantization and batching improve throughput per GPU, lowering cost per request.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable caching of repeated prompt prefixes: Disabling caching increases work.
• Increase maximum output tokens for every request: More tokens increase cost.
• Deploy one endpoint per user to isolate traffic: Per-user endpoints multiply cost.

Key takeaway: Quantize and batch to reduce inference cost.

stem: Notebook users must not be able to download training data to local machines or reach the internet. Which TWO controls help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Restrict S3 access to VPC endpoints with bucket policies
Grant notebook roles full S3 access to all buckets
Share one notebook user profile among all data scientists
Allow direct internet access from all notebook instances
Run SageMaker Studio in VPC-only mode without internet access

explanation:
Why this is correct:
VPC-only Studio and endpoint-restricted buckets limit data exfiltration paths.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Grant notebook roles full S3 access to all…: Full access increases exposure.
• Share one notebook user profile among all…: Shared profiles remove accountability.
• Allow direct internet access from all…: Internet access enables exfiltration.

Key takeaway: Limit data exfiltration from notebooks.

stem: A team wants to be notified when an endpoint's invocation errors exceed 1% over 10 minutes. Which approach fits?

choices.text: A Ground Truth labeling job reviewing failed requests each week
A CloudTrail trail recording the CreateEndpoint API only
A CloudWatch alarm using metric math on error and invocation metrics
A Model Monitor data quality schedule running once per month

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Metric math alarms can compute error rates from endpoint metrics.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A Ground Truth labeling job reviewing failed…: Labeling does not alert.
• A CloudTrail trail recording the…: CloudTrail records API calls.
• A Model Monitor data quality schedule…: Monthly data quality checks do not alert on errors.

Key takeaway: Alarm on error rates with metric math.

stem: Which feature restricts a SageMaker training container from making any outbound network calls, even inside a VPC?

choices.text: Warm pools for training clusters
Network isolation on the training job
Managed spot training on the job
Checkpointing to Amazon S3

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Network isolation blocks outbound network access from training containers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Warm pools for training clusters: Warm pools reuse infrastructure.
• Managed spot training on the job: Spot is a cost option.
• Checkpointing to Amazon S3: Checkpointing saves progress.

Key takeaway: Block container network access with network isolation.

stem: Repeated training experiments spend minutes provisioning instances each time. Which feature reduces startup time for iterative jobs?

choices.text: SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker batch transform
SageMaker managed warm pools
SageMaker Ground Truth

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Warm pools keep training infrastructure available between jobs, reducing startup latency.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SageMaker Model Monitor: Model Monitor watches endpoints.
• SageMaker batch transform: Batch transform is for inference.
• SageMaker Ground Truth: Ground Truth labels data.

Key takeaway: Speed iterative training with warm pools.

stem: Which option lets a SageMaker training job stream data directly from S3 in a sequential, high-throughput format without first downloading files?

choices.text: File mode with a large EBS volume
Loading data from the notebook's local disk
Manual download inside the training script only
Pipe input mode with RecordIO or similar formats

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Pipe mode streams data from S3 into the training container.

Why the other options are wrong:
• File mode with a large EBS volume: File mode downloads first.
• Loading data from the notebook's local disk: Notebook disks are not the training input.
• Manual download inside the training script only: Manual downloads add time.

Key takeaway: Stream training data with Pipe mode.

stem: A team wants to reduce model size and latency by training a smaller model to mimic a larger one. Which technique fits?

choices.text: Knowledge distillation
Feature crossing
Label smoothing regularization
Data augmentation

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Distillation trains a smaller student model to reproduce a larger teacher model's outputs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Feature crossing: Feature crossing creates feature interactions.
• Label smoothing regularization: Label smoothing regularizes targets.
• Data augmentation: Augmentation adds training variety.

Key takeaway: Shrink models with knowledge distillation.

stem: A classifier outputs probabilities that are poorly calibrated, and downstream systems depend on accurate probabilities. What should the team do?

choices.text: Increase the number of training epochs until the training loss reaches zero on every batch
Apply probability calibration, such as Platt scaling or isotonic regression
Remove the validation set so calibration cannot be measured
Report only the predicted class label without any probability

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Calibration methods adjust predicted probabilities to match observed frequencies.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Increase the number of training epochs until…: Longer training can worsen calibration.
• Remove the validation set so calibration…: Removing validation hides the problem.
• Report only the predicted class label…: Downstream systems need probabilities.

Key takeaway: Calibrate probabilities when they drive decisions.

stem: A team wants to deploy a Hugging Face model on SageMaker with a prebuilt, optimized inference container. Which option fits?

choices.text: Use an AWS Deep Learning Container or large model inference container
Package the model as an AWS Glue job for real time
Run the model inside an Amazon SQS message handler
Build a custom container from scratch with no base image and install every library by hand

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Prebuilt Deep Learning and LMI containers provide optimized runtimes for common frameworks.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Package the model as an AWS Glue job for…: Glue is for ETL.
• Run the model inside an Amazon SQS message…: SQS is not a model host.
• Build a custom container from scratch with…: Building from scratch is unnecessary work.

Key takeaway: Use prebuilt inference containers where possible.

stem: A company wants to prevent anyone from creating SageMaker notebooks with direct internet access in its accounts. Which preventive control fits?

choices.text: An email reminding data scientists about the internet access policy
A CloudWatch dashboard counting notebooks with internet access
An SCP or IAM condition requiring DirectInternetAccess to be disabled
A monthly review of notebook settings by the security team

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Condition keys in SCPs or IAM policies can deny creating notebooks with direct internet access.

Why the other options are wrong:
• An email reminding data scientists about the…: Reminders do not enforce.
• A CloudWatch dashboard counting notebooks…: Dashboards do not prevent.
• A monthly review of notebook settings by the…: Monthly reviews detect after the fact.

Key takeaway: Prevent risky notebook settings with policy conditions.
